newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cambodian parliament official rejects new premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian parliament official rejects new premier.

text.p: The second vice-president of the Cambodian parliament said on Thursday he did not approve of its election of a new first premier to replace the prince ousted in a bloody coup last month.
"A session of the National Assembly under the threat of weapons to me is not valid," Son Soubert said in a lecture in Tokyo. "I do not agree with the appointment of the new prime minister."
Under the rules of Cambodia's National Assembly, both vice presidents must approve certain motions, including the appointment of a new first prime minister.
On Wednesday, 86 members of the 120-seat assembly voted in favour of Ung Huot to replace Prince Norodom Ranariddh as first prime minister.

Son Soubert, a member of the Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party, Cambodia's third-largest political group, fled Cambodia after second prime minister Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh in a bloody coup in early July.
"I am not concerned with persons or personalities," Son Soubert said, "but more on the legal basis.
"If you don't respect all the legality, how can you hope for the Cambodian people to have democracy in their own country?"

Son Soubert arrived in Tokyo on Tuesday to seek Japan's help in ensuring that national elections due to be held in Cambodia next May are fair. He has had talks with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Shunji Yanai.
Son Soubert blamed both Hun Sen and Ranariddh for the crisis in Cambodia and demanded that both resign to ensure a fair election next year.
"The appointment of the first prime minister is not the way to solve the conflict in Cambodia. I believe it will only complicate the situation," he said.
"In my opinion, both prime ministers must go for the failure of management of the royal government."
Son Soubert's absence from Cambodia has brought into question the proper functioning of the assembly, but Hun Sen has said that those who have left Cambodia could not hold parliament hostage.
Son Soubert said he was ready to be dismissed from his post as the assembly was not functioning in a democratic fashion.
"I prefer to be dismissed," he said.

He said he hoped a meeting of foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Singapore on Monday would come up with measures to encourage the rival political parties to talk instead of using military force.
"It's important because if they give the wrong signal, Hun Sen will never compromise," he said.
Cambodia's scheduled membership in ASEAN was put on hold last month as a result of the coup.
